3) Are there tradeoffs we should call out for using prefix/KV caching with exported traces (impact on fidelity vs cost)?

Ellen / Marissa — quick technical responses inline: 

> 1) TLS & Authn: Our security team requires end-to-end TLS with mutual TLS for SIEM ingestion endpoints.

We can support mTLS from the forwarder to the SIEM. Options: 
- Customer-managed mTLS: the customer's PKI issues certs and we configure the forwarder to present a client cert to the SIEM. Rotation: automated via ACME-compatible flow or manual upload; we recommend ACME for frequent rotation.
- Relay termination: If the relay terminates TLS, we recommend re-encrypting with a separate client cert to the final SIEM. That allows inspection/forwarder-level routing but maintains end-to-end authenticity via delivery proofs described below.

> 2) Filtering: are filters applied at forwarder or exporter?

Filters in the sheet are implemented at the forwarder level (the component that runs inside the customer boundary). Rationale: keeps PII from leaving the enclave. The forwarder applies filters pre-batching, so compression and batching occur only on post-filtered data. We can expose a test mode to sample both pre- and post-filter outputs for validation.

> 3) Retention & Proof of Delivery: map delivery guarantees and idempotency

- Delivery model: at-least-once over TLS with persistent sequence ids. Forwarder keeps a local checkpoint for each flow until receipt ack from the SIEM endpoint.
- Idempotency: payloads include idempotency keys; SIEM side dedupe is recommended.
- Evidence: we can provide signed delivery receipts (sha256 over payload + timestamp, signed by Redwood HSM) as part of the evidence bundle for SOC2. Retention windows are configurable; default recommended: 90 days searchable, longer cold archives on request (365+).

Next steps I propose: 
- Kimberly: can you confirm whether 90 days is sufficient to sign off for Acme's SOC2 timeline, or if legal requires 365?
- Karthik: please attach a lightweight runbook for the forwarder cert rotation and the commands we'll run during the on-prem install.
